title: Release follow-ups before the first 0.1.0 publish: digest binding, negative-control specificity, wording (N1-N5)
description:
Carried from the Opus delta reviews of glyph-cli#94 (verdict APPROVE with non-blocking findings). Must land and be Opus-reviewed BEFORE the first real publish of 0.1.0. Workflow changes need their own Opus pass.
N1 release.yml (publish job, SHA256SUMS): SHA256SUMS travels in the same artifact as the tarball, so sha256sum -c proves only transfer integrity; the gate's own digest (scripts/check-package.mjs, printed) is never compared; the tag and publish steps pick the file with ls release/*.tgz separately from what the sums name, with no assertion of exactly one tarball. Pass the digest as a needs.package.outputs value and compare it; assert exactly one tarball.
N2 scripts/check-package.mjs negative control: the /dist\/glyph\.js/ regex matches four different rejections, so deleting the contents check leaves the control green. Match the message 'does not contain dist/glyph.js'.
N4 src/spawn.ts docstring says output overflow sets neither timedOut nor signal, but Node kills the child on maxBuffer so signal is probably SIGTERM: assert the real behaviour in scripts/node-spawn-check.mjs and fix the docstring.
N5 Wording that overstates: ADR 0007 around the dry-run and bytes claims, check-package.mjs header near line 215, and test/release-tag.test.ts (runs under Bun, say so).
Also still owed before 0.1.0, never an agent step: the first real dispatch (hosted-runner availability, OIDC and provenance line for GCLI-46 AC7) is the operator's tier-3 step.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the publish job compares the tarball sha256 produced by the Package job, passed as a needs.package.outputs value rather than read from the downloaded artifact, against the file it publishes (proof: workflow review by Opus plus a local mutation that alters the tarball after verification and goes red)
the publish job asserts exactly one .tgz in release/ and the tag check and publish steps use the same file path (proof: workflow review by Opus plus a mutation with two tarballs that goes red)
the negative control matches the message does not contain dist/glyph.js, and deleting the gate contents check turns the control red (proof: recorded mutation run)
scripts/node-spawn-check.mjs asserts the signal reported on maxBuffer overflow under node and the src/spawn.ts docstring states what it measured (proof: node-spawn-check output)
ADR 0007, check-package.mjs and release-tag.test.ts claims match what is proved (proof: Opus review of the diff)
the change landed with an Opus review before any publish dispatch (proof: review verdict recorded in the task notes)

the spawn tests are deterministic on the Linux runner: the spawn suite runs repeatedly in the Check job (or a recorded reason says why it does not) and the buffer-overflow race fixed in glyph-cli#97 cannot recur (proof: a CI step or a recorded repeated run on the Linux runner)

implementationNotes: Race found while landing glyph-cli#96: test/spawn.test.ts 'a buffer overflow is reported, not thrown' failed on the Linux runner (run 45079049186) because the child finished its single 100 kB write before the kill and exited 0. It passed on #94 and on macOS, so it is a test race, not a src/spawn.ts regression. Fixed in glyph-cli#97 (60243b2): the child now writes until killed. The determinism criterion was added to this task at the leader's instruction. Scope fence from the leader: no release.yml dispatch, no operator checklist change, no package.json private or version change.
